source_read: PMC HTML PMC8155734, full text (abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, strengths and limitations, conclusions, conflict and funding statements). Figure 1 (adjusted coefficients) and Figure 2 (LASSO ranks): screenshot of my tab came back blank, so figure image not viewable; nothing taken from them. Supplementary Figure 1 (unadjusted coefficients) and Supplementary Table 1 (missing data) are in the online supplement, not read.

claims.overstatement: (1) 'Women and men did not differ once dose per kilogram was allowed for' should be 'did not differ significantly': it is a non-significant adjusted coefficient, not a shown absence. (2) 'This design cannot separate sex from dose per kilogram' overstates the limit: dose per kilogram ranged 0.8 to 2.7 mg/kg and two doses were used, so the two are correlated rather than inseparable; 'cannot cleanly separate' fits. (3) 'For a rating of a bad drug effect, older age, trait anxiety and anxious-depressed mood before the dose ranked highest' is a LASSO ranking (single imputation, clustering ignored, no significance test); in the dose-adjusted mixed models the age association with bad drug effect did not survive correction for multiple testing (Discussion, 5th paragraph), and the claim should say so. (4) 'Bodies that differ are one reason people feel more or less from the same amount' is causal but rests on the authors' pharmacokinetic reasoning (dose per kilogram and CYP2D6 genotype to plasma level), which the data support reasonably; acceptable. No dosing advice; the doses are labelled as study conditions and the closing sentence is a proper caution.
claims.note: Parts not supported: (a) 'each took one capsule of MDMA' and 'just before the capsule': the 75 and 125 mg doses were prepared as gelatin capsules of 25 or 100 mg, so neither dose was one capsule; and 112 of the 194 (seven studies) took MDMA in two sessions, once alone and once after a medication pretreatment, with only the MDMA-alone session analysed. Suggest 'a single dose by mouth (capsules)'. (b) 'measured at screening' is stated for the NEO-FFI only; when the STAI trait scale was completed is not stated. (c) 'ranked first for 12, mostly pleasant and stimulating ones': the text names 6 of the 12 (VAS any drug effect, good drug effect, high mood, stimulated, liking; 5D-ASC oceanic boundlessness), all pleasant or stimulating; the other 6 are only in Figure 2 (not viewable), so 'mostly' cannot be checked. Numbers recomputed or found: 7 x 16 = 112, 112 + 24 + 28 = 164 at 125 mg and 30 at 75 mg (164/194 = 84.5%, the paper's 85%); 41 of 194 had used MDMA, so 79% were MDMA-naive (four in five: correct); all betas and semi-partial R2 values in statement and magnitude match the Results; R2 range 0.05 to 0.12 matches '5 to 12%'.

anchors.extracted: Pooled raw data from 10 double-blind placebo-controlled crossover studies, University Hospital Basel, 2009 to 2018, 194 healthy participants. Seven studies of 16 (112 people) gave 125 mg twice across four sessions (MDMA alone, MDMA after a medication pretreatment, placebo, pretreatment alone); three gave MDMA once (75 mg, n = 30; 125 mg, n = 24 and n = 28). Only MDMA-alone and placebo sessions analysed; washout at least 7 days; all registered.
Sessions in a quiet hospital research ward with no more than two research participants per session, lying in hospital beds, mostly listening to music; dosing fasting at 8 to 9 a.m.

194 healthy participants (97 female), aged 18 to 45 (mean 25.1, SD 4), from the University of Basel campus; weight 69 kg (SD 10; 46 to 97). Excluded: psychiatric history, physical illness, illicit drug use more than 10 times lifetime (cannabis excepted), any in the past 2 months or during the study; drug screens. 75 had used illicit drugs 1 to 8 times, 41 had used MDMA 1 to 5 times. NEO-FFI openness higher than norms (33.2 vs 24.5; t = 19.7).

anchors.locator: Methods > Study drug, 1st paragraph; Predictor variables, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Single oral dose of 75 or 125 mg MDMA hydrochloride prepared as gelatin capsules of 25 or 100 mg, as study conditions; same dose for women and men regardless of weight; dose per body weight 1.7 mg/kg (SD 0.4; 0.8 to 2.7); dose per kg used as covariate, which the authors say also accounts for the higher mg/kg in women.

anchors.locator: Methods > Predictor variables, 2nd to 6th paragraphs; Response variables, 4th paragraph
anchors.extracted: Predictors: sex, age, CYP2D6 genetic activity score, number of previous MDMA uses (0 to 5), AMRS mood scales rated before administration (including anxiety-depressiveness and introversion), NEO-FFI completed at screening, STAI trait scale (timing not stated); no expectation measure. 5D-ASC completed 6 h after dosing, rating the session retrospectively (three dimensions plus impaired control and cognition and anxiety subscales).

Multiple imputation (20 datasets); mixed models with random intercepts across studies; unadjusted and dose-per-kg-adjusted models; z-scored variables; semi-partial R2 (r2beta, Kenward-Roger); Benjamini-Hochberg correction across all tests (20 x 25 = 500, Figure 1 legend). LASSO with bootstrap-tuned penalty, single imputation, clustering ignored.

Unadjusted: plasma MDMA concentration associated with 16 of 24 outcomes uncorrected and 8 after correction; strongest with VAS any drug effect (beta 0.48, corrected p < 0.001, semi-partial R2 0.35), then mean arterial pressure 0.35, liking 0.36, good drug effect 0.35, stimulated 0.30, high mood 0.29.

Adjusted for dose per kg and corrected: sex no longer predicted plasma level; low CYP2D6 activity predicted higher plasma MDMA (beta -0.19, p < 0.001, R2 0.10); older age smaller heart-rate rise (-0.27, p = 0.019, R2 0.07); openness: closeness 0.28 (p = 0.019, R2 0.08), oceanic boundlessness 0.22 (p = 0.042, R2 0.06), visionary restructuralization 0.27 (R2 0.09), general inactivation -0.25 (R2 0.06); neuroticism and trait anxiety: dread of ego dissolution 0.32 and 0.32 (p = 0.001 and 0.004; R2 0.12 and 0.11), impaired control and cognition 0.26 and 0.26 (R2 0.08 and 0.07); anxiety-depressiveness and introversion before intake: 5D-ASC anxiety 0.25 and 0.23 (p = 0.042 each; R2 0.06 and 0.05).

LASSO: 8.6 predictors per response (5 to 13); dose per kg selected for 21 of 25 responses and largest for 12, named as the top predictor for VAS any drug effect, good drug effect, high mood, stimulated, liking and 5D-ASC oceanic boundlessness, less important for unpleasant or anxious reactions; for VAS bad drug effect older age ranked first, then trait anxiety, then pre-dose anxiety-depressiveness; neuroticism first for dread of ego dissolution and impaired control.

After adjustment for dose per kg, sex did not significantly influence MDMA effects; the authors attribute the stronger unadjusted response in women to lower weight and higher mg/kg, and note earlier studies that did find sex differences.

Older age with smaller temperature rise, less liking and good drug effect and more bad drug effect: these did not withstand correction for multiple testing; limited age range (people over 45 excluded).
Previous MDMA use showed no moderating effect; 79% were MDMA-naive and the rest had used it at most five times, so heavier use could not be assessed.
Anxiety scores after MDMA were small relative to other responses; only 7% reported anxiety as an acute adverse effect at 125 mg (citing an earlier analysis).

Young, mostly MDMA-naive healthy volunteers; possibly high openness; 85% received 125 mg; the physical and social setting could not be studied (highly standardized research setting with little variation); acute effects only.

key_findings.correction: Wording only: 'not significantly associated with any response after adjustment' is what the text shows (Discussion, 4th paragraph: did not significantly influence).

reporting_issues.note: Values confirmed as printed. Possibly not an error: r2beta semi-partial R2 is computed against variance not absorbed by the random study intercepts, so it can exceed the squared total-variance coefficient where studies differ in mean response; the card's advice not to quote them as shares of variance stands.

Studerus part confirmed (1-8 times under a more-than-10 exclusion vs 0-5 in Predictor variables, 4th paragraph); the comparison with the Vizeli and Liechti (2017) card was not checked (not my source).

PMC reference list marks Mithoefer et al. (2019), Psychopharmacology 236: 2735-2745, as [Retracted]; it is cited in the Introduction, 1st and 5th paragraphs. The DOI and the notice link were not visible in my text extraction.

risk_of_bias.note: ROBINS-E some concerns fits. One small point: the exposure-measurement domain says personality was measured at screening; the text says so for the NEO-FFI only, the STAI-T timing is not stated (does not change the judgment).

interpretation_gap.note: 'Minor' is defensible (accurate abstract, hedged practical conclusion), though the Discussion's 'led to' and the Conclusions' 'increased the likelihood' are causal. Gap (4) repeats the claim's 'cannot separate': with dose per kilogram ranging 0.8 to 2.7 mg/kg and two doses, sex and dose per kilogram are correlated, not inseparable; 'cannot cleanly separate' is more exact. Quoted Conclusions phrase is exact.

missed: 112 of the 194 (seven studies) also took MDMA in a second session after a medication pretreatment (Methods > Study design, 1st paragraph); the order of sessions is not given, so some MDMA-alone sessions may have followed an in-study MDMA exposure that the 'previous MDMA use' predictor does not count. Worth a line under exposure or limitations.

The 5D-ASC was completed 6 h after dosing as a retrospective rating of the session (Methods > Response variables, 4th paragraph); 'anxiety during the session' in the card and the claim is a same-day retrospective rating.
